summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was readmitted days after discharge due to worsening kidney function, recurrent diarrhea, and persistent neutropenia. She had recently been treated for ischemic colitis likely due to immunosuppressants, with a switch from mycophenolate mofetil to Myfortic. This admission revealed acute on chronic kidney injury, attributed to pre-renal causes and possible Bactrim toxicity, which improved with IV albumin and discontinuation of Bactrim. Diarrhea recurred despite Myfortic, and with negative stool studies, Myfortic was stopped. Neutropenia persisted but showed improvement after holding both Bactrim and Myfortic, with undetectable CMV viral load. Her condition stabilized, kidney function normalized, and she was discharged home with close outpatient follow-up, discontinuation of implicated medications, and continuation of core immunosuppression and supportive therapies.
